title: Quantum versus classical nonuniform advice
formal: Is \(\mathrm{BQP/qpoly}=\mathrm{BQP/poly}\) as classes of languages without an oracle? Explicitly, for every language decidable by a uniform polynomial-time quantum algorithm supplied with a polynomial-size quantum advice state depending only on input length, does some uniform polynomial-time quantum algorithm with polynomial-length classical advice decide the same language with error at most \(1/3\) on every input? The algorithm and polynomial advice bound may change. The reverse inclusion follows by encoding a classical advice string in the computational basis.
why: This compares the computational value of quantum and classical information stored in advance for an entire input length. It asks whether a short quantum state can support useful computations that no polynomial-length classical record can support, even when preparing either kind of advice is free. The shared-advice requirement makes this a different resource comparison from per-instance witnesses.

progress.text: Aaronson places quantum-advice bounded-error quantum computation inside PP with polynomial classical advice.
Aaronson–Kuperberg separate quantum and classical advice relative to a quantum oracle.
Li–Liu–Pelecanos–Yamakawa separate the advice classes relative to a classical oracle with classical-only access.
Bostanci–Huang–Vaikuntanathan give the first standard classical-oracle advice separation; the checked revision is dated 12 April.

status_note: Source-open for the ordinary total-language advice comparison. On 16 September 2026 the April 2026 ECCC revision’s definitions, Theorem 1.2 and advice discussion, Aaronson’s primary PP/poly upper-bound abstract, and the primary 2007 and 2024 oracle results were checked. A bounded later-work search found no unrelativized language-class resolution. The classically accessible, quantumly accessible classical, and unitary oracle models are distinguished. context_blocks.text: Advice is fixed before the particular input is seen and is trusted to be the chosen length-specific information. It must support every input of that length. A witness, by contrast, may be selected for one instance and must be checked against dishonest alternatives. Neither comparison is obtained simply by changing the name of the auxiliary register.

Quantum advice is supplied as a fresh copy on each run. The definition does not assume the algorithm can clone an unknown state or preserve it for unlimited reuse. Classical advice can be copied, but the class comparison allows either algorithm to consume the supplied resource during its computation.

The advice families can be uncomputable in both models. The question concerns what polynomial-size information makes possible for the uniform computation, not how to construct that information. Allowing input-specific advice would remove the crucial requirement that one message works for all strings of a given length.

Aaronson proved \(\mathrm{BQP/qpoly}\subseteq\mathrm{PP/poly}\). PP permits polynomial-time classical randomized computation with acceptance probability strictly greater than one half on yes-inputs and at most one half on no-inputs, without an inverse-polynomial margin; poly again permits length-specific classical advice. This upper bound uses a different computation model from bounded-error BQP, so it is not the desired simulation in BQP/poly.

The 2007 quantum-oracle separation demonstrated an advice advantage when both computations share a quantum black box. This supplies evidence in that augmented computation model and retains the oracle as an essential part of its statement.

The 2024 result separates the advice classes with an oracle encoding a classical function, but restricts even quantum algorithms to classical queries. This is a genuine precursor to the later standard classical-oracle theorem. Permitting superposition queries gives the classical-advice algorithm more power, so the access conventions must not be conflated.

The February 2026 construction, checked in its April revision, separates the advice classes using a standard classical oracle that both quantum algorithms may query in superposition. It resolves that oracle question while leaving the ordinary language equality asked here unresolved.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of \(\mathrm{BQP/qpoly}\subseteq\mathrm{BQP/poly}\), or a complete Lean-checked proof that some language has quantum advice as defined but no eligible classical-advice algorithm and family. An affirmative proof need not produce the classical advice efficiently, but must establish one length-indexed family and a uniform algorithm that work for all inputs. A negative proof must rule out every polynomial advice length, every classical advice family and every uniform quantum algorithm. A separation of promise problems alone does not automatically meet this card’s retained total-language target. Oracle separations, a difficult-to-describe state, or an advantage for advice selected after seeing the input do not suffice.
definitions: A language is a set \(L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*\); here every binary string must be decided, with no promise excluding some inputs. For each \(n\ge0\), let \(m(n),a(n)\) be nonnegative integers bounded by a fixed polynomial. A single deterministic classical Turing machine, given an input string \(x\) of length \(n\), generates in polynomial time a quantum circuit \(U_x\) with an \(m(n)\)-qubit advice register, \(a(n)\) ancillary qubits initialized to \(|0\rangle\), polynomially many gates, and one designated output qubit. The generating machine has no advice and no oracle. It uses the fixed exact gates \(H,T,\mathrm{CNOT}\), with \[H=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad T=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \mathrm{CNOT}|b,c\rangle=|b,b\mathbin\oplus c\rangle,\] where \(b,c\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\oplus\) is addition modulo two. The circuit outputs the computational-basis measurement of its output qubit. The quantum advice family is a sequence \((\rho_n)_{n\ge0}\) of density matrices on \(\mathbb C^{2^{m(n)}}\). A density matrix is positive semidefinite with trace one; positive semidefinite means \(v^\dagger\rho_nv\ge0\) for all vectors \(v\), and trace is the sum of diagonal entries. The probability of output 1 is \[\operatorname{Tr}\!\left[\Pi_1U_x\bigl(\rho_n\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|^{\otimes a(n)}\bigr)U_x^\dagger\right],\] where \(\Pi_1\) projects onto output 1 and is identity on the remaining qubits, and dagger denotes conjugate transpose. The language belongs to \(\mathrm{BQP/qpoly}\) if some such generating machine, polynomial bounds and advice family satisfy output-1 probability at least \(2/3\) for every \(x\in L\) and at most \(1/3\) for every \(x\notin L\). The same fixed \(\rho_n\) must work for all \(2^n\) strings of length \(n\). A fresh copy of that state is supplied for each independent computation; no cloning or repeated reuse of a consumed copy is promised. Advice is trusted: the requirement concerns the selected family, not all possible advice states. There is no computability or efficient-preparation requirement on the family, and its preparation cost is not charged. The language belongs to \(\mathrm{BQP/poly}\) if the advice can instead be a binary string \(b_n\in\{0,1\}^{m(n)}\), supplied as the basis state \(|b_n\rangle\). Its length may have a different polynomial bound and the circuit may be different, but \(b_n\) still depends only on \(n\), need not be computable, and must work for every length-\(n\) input. Both classes use uniform quantum computation in addition to the explicitly allowed nonuniform advice. BQP abbreviates bounded-error quantum polynomial time; poly and qpoly indicate classical-bit and quantum-qubit advice of polynomial length.

importance.reason: Asks whether quantum information can encode useful nonuniform computational advice beyond classical advice of comparable size.

category_assignment.reason: Mapped from the existing subject category

sentences: Quantum and classical advice supply information fixed for an entire input length to an efficient quantum computation.
The selected advice must decide every binary input of that length correctly with bounded error, and can be arbitrarily hard to prepare.
The question asks whether quantum advice increases the resulting ordinary class of total languages.
A known simulation by PP with classical advice uses a different error and computation model, while successive oracle separations retain their black boxes.
The latest standard classical-oracle separation does not resolve the ordinary equality, and fresh-copy advice remains distinct from untrusted per-instance witnesses.

source_formulation.text: Can every language decidable with polynomial-size quantum advice also be decided with polynomial-length classical advice, using an efficient quantum algorithm?
